findings.title: Discord User ID Hardcoded in Source Code
findings.description: The file .env.example and shared/lt1Presenters.ts contain a hardcoded Discord user ID (957974197953511524). While .env.example is intended as a template, including a real user ID in version-controlled files constitutes information disclosure. The same ID appears in lt1Presenters.ts as ownerDiscordId/discordId, making it part of the client-side bundle and publicly visible.
findings.recommendation: Use placeholder values in .env.example (e.g., YOUR_DISCORD_ID). For lt1Presenters.ts, consider whether Discord IDs need to be shipped to the client; if not, keep them server-side only.

findings.title: In-Memory Rate Limiting Bypassed Across Serverless Invocations
findings.description: The rate limiter in api/_lib/rateLimit.ts uses an in-memory Map. On Vercel (serverless), each invocation may run in a separate container, meaning the rate limit state is not shared across instances. An attacker can bypass rate limits by triggering enough concurrent requests to hit different cold-start instances.
findings.recommendation: Use a distributed rate limiting solution such as Upstash Redis or Vercel KV for production rate limiting. The in-memory store should only be used for local development.

findings.title: In-Memory Vote Store Allows Duplicate Votes in Production Without KV
findings.description: The voteStore.ts uses an in-memory Set as fallback when KV is not configured. In non-production environments this silently allows duplicate votes across serverless instances. In production it throws an error, which is correct, but the development fallback could mask issues during testing.
findings.recommendation: Log a warning in development that vote deduplication is unreliable without KV. Consider requiring KV in staging environments to catch issues before production.

findings.title: OAuth Callback Uses GET Method for State-Changing Operation
findings.description: The OAuth callback handler (api/auth/callback.ts) processes the authorization code exchange via GET request. While this is standard for OAuth2 authorization code flow, the GET request triggers a session cookie creation (state-changing side effect). Browser prefetching or link scanners could potentially trigger unintended token exchanges, though the state parameter mitigates replay.
findings.recommendation: This is acceptable per OAuth2 spec but consider adding Cache-Control: no-store (already present) and ensuring the state token is single-use. The current implementation clears the state cookie after use, which is correct.

findings.title: Session Cookie Uses SameSite=Lax Instead of Strict
findings.description: Session cookies are set with SameSite=Lax. This means cookies are sent on top-level navigations from external sites (e.g., clicking a link). While Lax is required for the OAuth callback flow, the session cookie could use Strict after the initial login redirect completes.
findings.recommendation: SameSite=Lax is reasonable for OAuth flows. The CSRF protection via Origin/Referer header validation in requestGuard.ts provides an additional defense layer. No immediate action required, but consider Strict for higher security if OAuth flow permits.

findings.title: Logout Endpoint Lacks CSRF Token (Relies on Origin Check Only)
findings.description: The logout endpoint (api/auth/logout.ts) enforces CSRF via Origin/Referer header matching but does not use a per-request CSRF token. While Origin-based CSRF protection is generally effective, some older browsers or proxy configurations may strip Origin headers, potentially allowing CSRF-based forced logout.
findings.recommendation: The current Origin/Referer check is a reasonable defense. For defense-in-depth, consider adding a double-submit cookie or synchronizer token pattern for state-changing POST requests.

findings.title: Custom Session Token Implementation Instead of Standard JWT/Library
findings.description: The session management in api/_lib/session.ts implements a custom signed token format (v1.<base64payload>.<hmac>) rather than using an established library like jose or iron-session. While the implementation appears correct (HMAC-SHA256, timing-safe comparison, expiry check), custom crypto implementations carry inherent risk of subtle bugs.
findings.recommendation: Consider using a well-audited library for session token creation and verification. The current implementation is functionally sound but a library would reduce maintenance burden and provide broader community review.

findings.title: YouTube Embed URL Injected from Environment Variable Without Validation
findings.description: In src/Pages/LT1.tsx, the iframe src is set directly from import.meta.env.VITE_YOUTUBE_PR_VIDEO_URL without validating that the URL points to a legitimate YouTube domain. A misconfigured environment variable could embed arbitrary content. However, the CSP frame-src directive in vercel.json restricts frames to youtube.com and youtube-nocookie.com, which mitigates this at the browser level.
findings.recommendation: Add application-level validation that the URL matches expected YouTube embed patterns (e.g., https://www.youtube.com/embed/ or https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/). The CSP provides defense-in-depth but explicit validation is better practice.

findings.title: External Link Missing rel='noopener' Attribute
findings.description: The Button component (src/Components/ui/Button.tsx) uses rel='noreferrer' for external links but does not explicitly include 'noopener'. Modern browsers include noopener behavior with target='_blank' by default, but explicit declaration is a best practice.
findings.recommendation: Change rel='noreferrer' to rel='noopener noreferrer' for defense-in-depth. Note: noreferrer implies noopener in modern browsers, so this is a minor style improvement.

findings.title: Trusted Proxy Verification Relies on Spoofable Headers
findings.description: In api/_lib/trustedIp.ts, the Vercel provider trusts x-forwarded-for only when x-vercel-id is present, and Cloudflare trusts cf-connecting-ip only when cf-ray is present. While these verification headers add a layer of protection, they could theoretically be spoofed if the application is not behind the expected proxy. The TRUST_PROXY flag defaults to false, which is correct.
findings.recommendation: Ensure the deployment platform (Vercel/Cloudflare) strips or overwrites these headers on incoming requests before they reach the application. Document that TRUST_PROXY must only be enabled when the application is exclusively accessed through the configured proxy.

findings.title: Rate Limit Bucket Pruning Threshold Could Allow Memory Growth
findings.description: The rate limiter only prunes expired entries when the bucket Map exceeds 5000 entries. Under sustained attack with many unique keys, memory could grow up to 5000 entries before pruning occurs. In a serverless context with short-lived instances this is unlikely to be a practical issue.
findings.recommendation: Consider lowering the pruning threshold or implementing periodic cleanup. In the serverless context (Vercel), this is a low concern since instances are ephemeral.

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy Missing 'unsafe-inline' Restriction Verification
findings.description: The CSP in vercel.json sets script-src 'self' and style-src 'self', which is good. However, React and Tailwind (via Vite) may require additional directives depending on the build output. If the build generates inline styles or scripts, the page may break or require CSP adjustments. The current policy appears well-configured for a Vite+React SPA.
findings.recommendation: Verify that the production build works correctly with the current CSP. Consider adding a report-uri or report-to directive to catch CSP violations in production.

findings.title: GitHub Actions Uses Pinned Commit Hashes (Positive Finding)
findings.description: The GitHub Actions workflow pins actions to specific commit SHAs rather than mutable tags, which is a security best practice that prevents supply chain attacks via tag reassignment.
findings.recommendation: No action needed. This is a positive security practice. Continue pinning action versions to commit SHAs.
